newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK overnight rates close firmer on stock demand.
newsitem.headline: HK overnight rates close firmer on stock demand.

text.p: Overnight rates closed firmer on Friday on demands for the public offering of two Hong Kong listed stocks, but trading was calm and orderly, dealers said.
Overnight money ended at five 4-3/8 percent after touching a low of 4-3/8 1/4. It was at 4-5/16 3/16 on Thursday.
"Trading was volatile and demands for IPO settlements lifted overnight rates in the afternoon," a local bank dealer said.
Timber products processor Ta Fu International Holdings Ltd closed its public share offering on Thursday and Shandong Xinhua Pharmaceutical Co Ltd completed sales on Friday.
Three-month money was virtually unchanged at 5-9/16 1/5 percent.
Government paper yields followed U.S. treasuries and were generally easier in thin trade.
Three-year note yields fell to 6.08 percent from 6.18, the seven-year yield edged down to 7.06 percent from 7.18 and the longest 10-year note yielded 7.31 percent versus 7.42.
One-month yields eased two basis points to 4.32 percent.
But the one-week bill was affected by higher overnight rates, yielding 4.25 percent, up slightly from 4.22 on Thursday.
